{"self_assessment": "Impact: I drew the scratch-pad sketch that the whole table built from. It set the fish outline, with the two body strokes numbered so Tom and Leo could each take a line right away. I then redrew the tail with soft curves instead of sharp corners, so the fall could carry through it. I also fetched 40 dominoes for the shared bin early, so nobody ran short while building. I laid the top tail myself, tracing it onto the end of the top line.

Execution: I worked the sketch to match what dominoes can actually do: rounded corners, gentle flares, and lines that all leave the start in the same direction. I ran a dry-run on the design. I then built part of the top tail by tracing from the pad. After the build I ran four close inspections of the run, including the nose joint, to check the push would reach everything. I reported what I saw back to the table so the team could decide whether anything needed fixing.

Collaboration: I took Maya's feedback on the tail and redrew it until the pad showed a design she was happy with. I split the work clearly, with Tom and Leo on the body strokes, Maya on the tail and nose, and me on the pad and top tail, so nobody doubled up. I kept my hands out of other people's areas to avoid bumps, and I shared my inspection findings openly.

Leadership: I set the plan early by choosing the stroke numbering and who builds what. I steered the table toward a hands-off finish once the run looked connected, to reduce the risk of a late bump, and I kept the team focused and upbeat through the final minutes. I briefed the manager on our status. I can't see the result of the fall from here, so I'm not claiming the outcome, but the design and build process were sound.", "my_share_percent": 30}
